summary: Sanders County, MT steel lookout on the National Bison Range; firelookout.com gives 72 ft, 1934 plans said 60 ft; listed gone, with no date or site description.

facts.status_note: firelookout.com and the FFLA Montana list both mark the tower gone; neither gives a date or cause
facts.agency: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service (National Bison Range)

access.note: No source describes what remains at the site or whether visitors can reach it

events.note: February 1934 Missoulian item, quoted by the Forest Lookouts page: a crew was erecting three 60-foot steel towers on the Bison Range, one planned for Wild Horse Mesa

evidence.supports: steel tower, 72 feet per firelookout.com, dated to the 1930s, 1/2 mile south of summit, now gone
evidence.quote: 1930s: 72' steel tower 1/2 mile south of summit. Gone.

evidence.supports: location about 7 miles west of St. Ignatius, Sanders County
lookout listed under the National Bison Range
1934 crew erecting three 60-foot steel towers for lookout fire stations
evidence.quote: erection of three 60-foot steel towers for lookout fire stations

evidence.supports: planned sites included Wild Horse Mesa
evidence.quote: They are to be located at High Point, Wild Horse Mesa, and Thumb-Nob.

evidence.supports: FFLA Montana list marks the Wild Horse Mountain tower gone
evidence.quote: Wild Horse Mountain Sanders 47.31501 -114.24459 Tower Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives a 72-foot steel tower (about 21.9 m). A February 1934 item quoted by the Forest Lookouts page describes three 60-foot steel towers being erected, one for Wild Horse Mesa. The brief's 18.3 m matches the 60-foot figure. No source gives the finished height, so height_m is left out.

notes_for_editor: Two lookout pages and the FFLA list only. No staffing, fire, removal date or site photo found. The 72 ft vs 60 ft height conflict is unresolved; check the brief's 18.3 m against a second source. The 1934 item describes towers still being erected, so it may not give the finished size. The Bison Range history and NHLR had no entry for this site in the cache.
